Leave resolve_role_in_tx/1 UNCHANGED (design section 3 explicitly scopes it out -- zero current callers, correct fix depends on a not-yet-built S3 caller). In lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex: handle_list_roles/1 -> handle_list_roles/2 (route macro passes conn.assigns.scoped_opts as second arg; body calls RoleRegistry.list_roles(opts)); handle_upsert_role/1 -> handle_upsert_role/2 (same shape; body calls RoleRegistry.upsert_role(name, group_id, opts)). No other change to either file's validation logic, response-shaping, or error-mapping.

MANDATORY, per ISS-0768's own acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0768.yaml) -- investigate and RECORD whether this is a regression or has been broken since RoleRegistry shipped. Run the exact git commands specified in the design doc's section 4 (git log -p --follow -S"prefix" -- lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex, and the introduction-commit check) against this worktree's history, and write the actual finding (with commit SHAs if a regression, or 'no commit in history ever threaded prefix: -- broken since introduction' if not) into your result.summary. This is not optional and not a formality -- ORCH will check your result names a specific SHA-backed finding, not a restatement of the design doc's instructions.

Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and the full mix test suite (at minimum test/letflow/identity/role_registry_test.exs and any test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs) and quote real output in your result -- never a prediction. Do not write the NEW cross-tenant-isolation regression test yourself -- that is TEST-DESIGNER's job at step-05; you are only responsible for making the EXISTING suite compile and pass against the new arities.

Branch feature/WF03-ISS0768-20260921 is checked out in this worktree (c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\letflow-wf03-iss0768) -- work there, do not touch c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\letflow (a different concurrent session owns uncommitted work there on an unrelated issue).
